title: Hidden view · How Gerard shows through what hides him
description: The ways a building can let Gerard show through when it stands between him and the camera, shot from the same spots: the earlier ring cut, the dithered window (Baldur's Gate 3, Divinity: Original Sin 2), the ghost screen door (Diablo) and the building left whole with a silhouette (Torchlight). With the camera fixed (?camara=fija; camera-orbit shows it turning). The style is window.gerard.game.occlusion.style (?cut=), silhouettes window.gerard.game.occlusion.silhouettes (?silueta=0).

steps.eval: window.cutOpen = () => window.gerard.game.app.root.findByName('Entorno: meridiana-calle').find(e => !!e.render).flatMap(e => e.render.meshInstances).map(m => m.getParameter('geoCutOpen')?.data).filter(r => r !== undefined); window.cutSettled = () => window.cutOpen().every(r => r === 0 || r === 1);

steps.caption: On a crossing behind a tall block · Before: a cut of 5 m radius traced by a glowing edge, wider towards the camera
On a crossing behind a tall block · Dithered window (new default): a circle of 3.3 m radius round Gerard on screen, its rim dissolving, with silhouettes
On a crossing behind a tall block · Ghost: the whole building turns to a screen door, with silhouettes
On a crossing behind a tall block · Silhouette only: the building stays whole and Gerard and Aitor show through it

steps.eval: const n = window.gerard.game.app.scene.layers.getLayerByName('World').meshInstances.filter(m => m.material?.name === 'Silueta').length; if (n < 20 || n > 70) throw new Error(`Gerard and Aitor should have 20–70 silhouette parts, not ${n}`);
